indications_and_usage: Epinephrine is indicated in the emergency treatment of allergic reactions (Type I) including anaphylaxis to stinging and biting insects, foods, drugs, and other allergens.
dosage_and_administration: Inject intramuscularly or subcutaneously into the anterolateral aspect of the thigh. Do not inject into digits, hands, or feet.
contraindications: There are no absolute contraindications to the use of epinephrine in a life-threatening situation.
warnings_and_precautions: Epinephrine should be administered with caution in patients who have heart disease, including arrhythmias, coronary artery or organic heart disease, or hypertension.
drug_interactions: Patients receiving cardiac glycosides, diuretics, or antiarrhythmics should be observed carefully for the development of cardiac arrhythmias if given epinephrine.
The effects of epinephrine may be potentiated by tricyclic antidepressants and monoamine oxidase inhibitors.
use_in_specific_populations: Epinephrine should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
pregnancy: Teratogenic Effects: Epinephrine has been shown to have teratogenic effects when given to animals in doses several times human doses.
pediatric_use: Epinephrine may be administered to pediatric patients at a dosage appropriate to body weight.
geriatric_use: Clinical studies did not include sufficient numbers of subjects aged 65 and over. Older patients may be more sensitive to the effects of sympathomimetic agents.
overdosage: Overdosage may cause sharp rise in blood pressure, cerebrovascular hemorrhage, pulmonary edema, ventricular arrhythmias, and renal failure.
adverse_reactions: Common adverse reactions include anxiety, apprehensiveness, restlessness, tremor, weakness, dizziness, sweating, palpitations, and pallor.
